# Mine

A set of small PWAs that keep your personal data as markdown in a private GitHub repo —
calendar, zettelkasten, diary — so it stays portable and free of vendor lock-in.

**Live: https://maximilianharr.github.io/mine/** — install it to your home screen.

## Docs

| | |
| --- | --- |
| [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) | what the app does and how it behaves |
| [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) | how it is built, and the verified platform findings |
| [TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md](TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md) | what is checked before a change ships, and how |
| [calendar/](calendar/) | the calendar app, with its own pair of docs |

## Layout

```
index.html app.js style.css sw.js manifest.json   the main app
shared/   apps.js store.js github.js md.js        used by every app
          markdown.js prefs.js vendor/
calendar/                                         one folder per app
spike/                                            on-device platform checks
test/                                             the checks: test/run.sh
```

No build step: no bundler, no CI, no dependencies to install. `git push` deploys to GitHub
Pages. To run it locally, `python3 -m http.server` in this folder and open the printed URL.
`test/run.sh` runs the model checks in node and the rest in a headless browser, and installs
nothing either.

Data lives in a **separate private repo**, never in this one. The token is entered once in the
app, stored on the device, and scoped so it can only touch that data repo.

## Status

The main app, the sync layer and the on-device checks are done and verified end to end against a
real repo. The calendar is built — the five views, the kanban, the entry popup and its field
popups, the filter and the settings — and `test/run.sh` covers it.

Not built yet: the per-app summary above the tiles that [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md)
describes. The tile screen shows tiles only, so opening the calendar is currently the only way
to see what is on today.

once there is something to save, and an `x` to close. On an entry that already exists the type is
a **marker, not a choice** — a ticked square for a task, a calendar page for an event, shown and
not pressable — because a task turned into an event drops its stage, its importance and its
estimate, and the type is settled when the entry is made. On a new entry it is the pair, with the
event selected.

The trashcan stays at the left of that group: deleting is not an edit of a field, it writes at
once whatever the draft holds, and the board's rule that a card is deleted from its popup in two
taps depends on the trashcan being on the first of them.

Below the row, in this order: the **title**, the **scope and skip** row on a repeating entry, the
**when**, the **toggle row**, the **five field rows**, and the **details body** last.

### A row, and a row being edited

Every row is **the icon, then the value** — no field name beside it:

```
[ball]    Work                                      [trash]
[pin]     Conference room 3B                        [trash]
[repeat]  Repeat
[bell]    Alerts
```

live from the start. The disk creates the file; until it is pressed, a `+` opened and thought
better of leaves no file and no commit.

**The disk is disabled until the title has something in it**, because an entry must have one.
That is the only way a new entry differs from an edit of a saved one, and it is a disabled button
rather than a rule about which row may be touched first.

### A repeating entry

A repeating entry says so under the title, and carries two things the rest do not:

- **the scope pair**, `this occurrence` or `whole series`, which governs **what the save
  writes**. It is one choice about one write, which is what it always was; it is here rather than

  resets what a discard is measured against.
- **`skip this one`**, which drops a single occurrence. That is an action on the entry like
  deleting it, not a change to a field, so it sits with the scope rather than among the rows.

Only the series carries the rule, so **the repetition row is absent on an occurrence override** —
a rule the popup must not rewrite has no row at all.

### Saving, and leaving

The disk **closes the popup and returns to the calendar immediately**; the push to GitHub runs in
the background and is reported in the sync line, not in the popup. **Both ways out land on the
calendar**, the disk and the `x` alike. The cell or the card behind it shows the result anyway,
and there is no preview left to step back to.

Deleting the entry and skipping an occurrence also close the popup, because neither leaves
anything to look at.

**Leaving a popup that holds unsaved changes asks first.** The popup's `x`, a click on the
backdrop and Escape are one way out and ask one question: a small centred prompt offering

I've read `calendar/popup.js`, `calendar/index.html`, `calendar/data.js`, `calendar/app.js`, the CSS and the three docs plus `test/check.mjs`. Here's the ground truth I'll build on, so I don't ask you things the code already answers:

- `#popup` is a real `<form id="entry-form">`. Enter in any single-line input inside it **submits the form** → `collect()` + save + `discard()`. That's your "closes the ticket".
- The inline inputs inside the form are exactly four: **title, alerts, location, participants**. The **body is a `<textarea>`** in the form — Enter there inserts a newline and never submits.
- The when / estimate / category / repeat controls live in `#fpop`, a div **outside** the form, so Enter there does nothing at all today.
- The scope pair + `skip this one` is `scopeRow()` (`.scope` → `.scope-note` + `.vrep` → `.btngroup` of two `.seg` + the skip `.link`), rendered between the title row and the when row, only when `D.occ.seriesId` is set.
- The top row is `#f-icons` via `iconRow()`: type marker → `spacer` → trash → disk (when dirty) → x.
- The trashcan today **always deletes the whole series** (`deleteEntry(occ.seriesPath)`), with a confirm that says "Its override files stay behind."
- `skipOccurrence(occ)` pushes `occ.recId` onto the series' `exdate` and rewrites the rule file with `move:false`. It does **not** touch an existing override file.
- `bodyEditor` wraps the textarea in `field('Notes', t, 'Raw markdown — exactly what lands in the file.')`.
- `test/check.mjs:1446-1466` asserts the "repeating" note, exactly 1 skip button, 2 `.seg`, and the `.scope` block's position. Those tests will have to change.

A recurring file states the rule only. Anything that happens to a *single* occurrence — ticked,
moved, retitled, cancelled — is an override file in the date tree carrying `series:` and
`recurrence-id:`, holding only the keys that differ. The rule file is never rewritten, and since
each override is a fresh path it cannot conflict, even when two devices do it offline.

`exdate:` covers a plain skip where there is nothing to record.

## Rendering a range

1. Collect dated entries whose `start` falls in the range.
2. Expand every rule in `recurring/` over the range; drop dates in `exdate`, add `rdate`.
3. Replace an occurrence with the override matching `series` + `recurrence-id`; an override
An unknown zone name falls back to the device's rather than throwing, because a bad value in
settings must not stop the calendar rendering.

## Writes from the popup

The popup holds a draft and writes once. The disk is `createEntry` on a new entry, `updateEntry`
on a saved one, and `saveOverride` when the scope pair says `this occurrence` — so **one entry
edit is one commit**, and the occurrence the popup was opened with stays valid for as long as the
popup is open, because nothing has moved under it.

**Per-row write-through was considered and rejected**, and the reasons are worth keeping, because
each of them is invisible until it bites:

- the popup would have to re-point at the saved entry after every write. `S.reload()` rebuilds
  the model, so the occurrence held by the popup is a generation stale the moment a row saves,
  and its `baseOid` with it. The row that saved looks perfectly correct — it put the value there
  itself — and the *next* row's save goes out against a dead base and lands as a conflict against
  a file the user just wrote;
- a date change moves the file, the day being in the path and the API having no rename, so the
  popup would have to follow the entry to a new path mid-edit or write to one that no longer
  exists;
- several saves can queue before a drain, offline or faster than the chain runs, and
  `POST /git/trees` is handed one entry per queued item — so the same path would appear more than
  once in one tree, which the save-once popup cannot produce.

A draft has none of these, and the only thing it gives up is that the popup shows a value the
file does not yet hold. The disk appearing exactly when the two differ is what says so.

**`snapshot(D)` is what the disk and the prompt both read.** It already exists for the discard
prompt: the draft's editable parts, serialised, compared against the baseline taken when the
popup opened. The disk's presence is the same comparison, so there is one definition of *changed*
and not two to drift apart — a disk that shows when the prompt would stay silent, or the reverse,
is that one function having grown a second copy.

Switching the scope pair rebuilds the draft from the other file and **must retake the baseline**.
A baseline left behind reads as changed, which puts a disk in the top row of a popup nobody has
edited and makes every way out ask about changes nobody made.

Committed as `ce83ac5` on `main`, not pushed.

## What shipped

**Enter / Shift+Enter** — one delegated `keydown` on `#f-rows` (`calendar/popup.js:200`). Enter in the title, alerts, location, participants or the details textarea calls `closeRow()` and prevents the default; `e.shiftKey` bails out first, so the textarea's newline is the browser's own and cost no code. `#fpop` is outside `#f-rows`, so field popups are untouched.

**The scope pair** — now built by `scopePair()` into `#f-icons`, right of the type marker, reading `this` / `all` with `aria-label="This occurrence"` / `"All occurrences"`. `scopeRow()`, the "Part of a repeating entry." line, `skip this one`, and the `.scope` / `.scope-note` / `.vrep` CSS are gone; `.iconbar .seg` is `flex: none` so the row can't wrap.

**The trashcan** — reads the pair: `all` deletes the rule file as before, `this` calls `skipOccurrence()`, which now also removes the occurrence's override file in the same commit. Both confirm, worded by scope.

**The details row** — `bodyEditor` returns the bare textarea with `aria-label="Details"`. `field()` stays for `whenEditor` and `recurrenceEditor`.

Plus `sw.js` → `2026-11-24.2`.

## Verification

`test/run.sh` green, 0 failures, across two full runs. I repaired the five assertions your change invalidated and added 35, including:

- Enter leaves the popup open, closes its row, keeps the typed title, and writes nothing — pressed through CDP's `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`, because implicit form submission is native and a synthetic `KeyboardEvent` can't trigger it, so couldn't prove it had stopped.
- Shift+Enter leaves the body row open with `'first\n'` in the textarea.
- Enter inside `#fpop` closes neither popup.
- The pair is in the top row, right of the marker, on one line with the `x` **at 360px as well as 900px** — the wrap risk was only on a phone, so the desktop measurement alone wouldn't have caught it.
- Trash + `this` asks `Skip "Water the plants" on YYYY-MM-DD?`, then leaves the rule file in place with an `exdate` added; trash + `all` asks about the whole entry, still warns about override files, and the file is gone. `confirm()` is stubbed and the question read back, which is the only way to check the wording.

Docs updated: `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md` (7 passages), `calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` (2), `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` (the repeating-entry section rewritten, three new ones).

## Two things to flag

**You changed your own spec twice during the interview, and I built what you landed on.** You asked for `'this event'` / `'all events'`; the only repeating entry anywhere in the fixture is a *task* (`Water the plants`, generated by `test/serve.py`), so you went type-neutral and then shorter still — `this` / `all`. If you want the nouns back, it's one ternary in `scopePair()`.

**One pre-existing hazard got more exposed and I left it alone, as you decided.** Switching the pair runs `D = draft(...)` then `D.clean = snapshot(D)`, so unsaved typing is discarded with no prompt and no trace. That was always true, but the pair now sits a thumb's width from the disk and the x rather than below the title, so a mis-tap is likelier. Reusing the existing `#ask` prompt would be ~15 lines if you change your mind.
